lens: HPC lossy-compression expert (SZ3/ZFP internals). WHY SZ3/ZFP WIN BY 3-5 ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE — four compounding causes, verified against the code. (1) ERROR DOMAIN AND ACCUMULATION: TRACQ quantizes percent-changes computed OPEN-LOOP from the original data (core_enhanced.py:_compute_raw_percent_grid) and reconstructs by cumprod (reconstruct_from_quantized, line ~634). A per-step quantization error delta_t in log-value space performs a random walk: Var[log X_hat[t] - log X[t]] ~ t * sigma_q^2, so RMSE grows like sqrt(t) times the per-step error at best, and diverges when clamping/mu-law bias makes E[delta] != 0 (MetroPT-3 RMSE 3.8e95 over 1.5M steps is exactly this: a tiny multiplicative bias raised to the 1.5-millionth power). SZ3's predictor operates on DECODED values (closed-loop DPCM): the decoder's prediction error can never exceed one quantization bin, so per-point error is bounded by the user's epsilon with ZERO accumulation, at ANY series length, with no anchors. This alone is worth 2-4 orders of magnitude on long series. (2) QUANTIZER RESOLUTION: TRACQ 8-bit with a per-variable clamp C_i of tens-to-hundreds of percent gives a coarsest step of ~2C/255, i.e. ~0.4-4% RELATIVE error PER STEP, before compounding; SZ3 at abs=1e-3 on O(100)-magnitude data delivers 1e-5 relative error, bounded. Mu-law reshapes but cannot shrink this: 8 bits is 8 bits. (3) ENTROPY STAGE WORKS AGAINST ITSELF: mu-law companding is DESIGNED to equalize occupancy of the 256 levels, so the PNG DEFLATE stage (codec.py) sees a near-max-entropy byte stream and compresses almost nothing — the measured lossy ratios (0.05-0.22) barely beating lossless Delta+Zstd (0.12-0.24) is the smoking gun. SZ3 does the opposite: it predicts first so quantization indices pile up in a few bins near zero (typical entropy 0.3-2 bits/value on smooth data), then Huffman+Zstd harvests that skew; ZFP decorrelates 4^d blocks with a near-orthogonal lifted transform and spends bits by bit-plane significance. (4) NO ERROR BOUND / OUTLIER HANDLING: TRACQ's clamp silently destroys large excursions (unbounded pointwise error at clipped pixels) and near-zero denominators blow up percent-change; SZ3 stores unpredictable points EXACTLY (outlier fallback), so max-error <= epsilon holds for every point. KEY STRUCTURAL INSIGHT that makes the fix implementable in numpy: closed-loop DPCM with a uniform quantizer on a FIXED VALUE LATTICE is algebraically identical to (a) snapping values to the lattice open-loop, then (b) integer-differencing the lattice indices. Integer cumsum at decode is EXACT, so all drift vanishes while everything stays vectorized — no sequential per-step loop needed. And the integer difference grid IS a per-timestep 2D relative-change image: SZ3's internal quantization-index field, rendered as the TRACQ artifact. ANSWER TO THE KEY QUESTION: yes — SZ3-class rate-distortion is achievable inside the TRACQ grid framework, because SZ3's core (Lorenzo prediction + error-bounded linear quantization + entropy coding) maps exactly onto an integer-index image; the residual gap to SZ3 is only the entropy coder (DEFLATE/Zstd vs tuned Huffman+Zstd, ~10-30% rate) and SZ3's per-block regression predictor (minor on 1D-per-row time series). ZFP-class transform coding maps less naturally and is not needed to win.
overall_assessment: Proposal 1 (lattice-quantized, error-bounded change grid) is the single change that matters — it removes the sqrt(T)-to-exponential error accumulation that costs TRACQ 3-5 orders of magnitude, replaces the clamp/mu-law/anchor machinery with a provable per-point bound, and simultaneously creates the peaked residual distribution the entropy stage needs. Alone it converts TRACQ from 'never Pareto-optimal' to ZFP-competitive; nothing else on the list works without it, and mu-law/anchors must be retired when it lands (they conflict). I would ship 1+2+3 as one coherent codec, 'TRACQ-EB': lattice quantization with user-specified abs/rel error bound (1), escape-coded exact-outlier sidecar for the guarantee and for near-zero channels (3), and per-row predictor selection {order-1, order-2, 2D-Lorenzo} on the integer lattice with a centered uint8 residual image entropy-coded by Zstd (PNG kept as the viewable artifact) (2). Proposal 4 (per-variable domain/bin selection) is a cheap tuning layer worth adding once 1-3 benchmark green; Proposal 5 (ZFP-style block transform) should be prototyped last and dropped if it does not beat 2D-Lorenzo, which I expect on sensor time series. Honest benchmark expectation on UCI Air Quality: TRACQ-EB at abs eps=0.007 should land near RMSE 4e-3 at ratio 0.10-0.18 vs ZFP's 4e-3 at 0.273 — a genuine win — and should sit within ~1.3x of SZ3's rate at equal RMSE; on MetroPT-3 the divergence disappears by construction and TRACQ-EB becomes Pareto-competitive among per-timestep-resolution methods (PAA-1024 remains cheaper only because it discards 1023 of every 1024 samples, which the brief's core-idea constraint already rules out as a comparison class).

proposals.name: Lattice-quantized error-bounded change grid (closed-loop-equivalent, drift-free)
proposals.mechanism: Replace the open-loop percent-change + mu-law + cumprod pipeline with quantization on a fixed value lattice. User specifies an error bound. ABS mode: v[i,t] = round(X[i,t] / (2*eps_abs)) (int64). REL mode (this IS the relative-change grid, formalized): v[i,t] = round(log|X[i,t]| / log(1 + 2*eps_rel)) with per-channel sign handling or the existing auto-offset to keep channels positive. The stored grid is the integer first difference d[i,t] = v[i,t] - v[i,t-1] — one pixel per variable per timestep, each pixel a quantized (relative) change, exactly TRACQ's artifact. Decode: v = cumsum(d, axis=1) + v[:,0]; X_hat = 2*eps*v (abs) or sign*(1+2*eps_rel)^v (rel). Because cumsum over integers is exact, reconstruction error equals the per-point snapping error: |X - X_hat| <= eps_abs (or relative error <= eps_rel) at EVERY point, independent of T. This is algebraically identical to closed-loop DPCM with a uniform quantizer (the classic SZ construction), but fully vectorizable — no sequential encoder loop. Anchors, mu-law, adaptive clamp, and the 8/16-bit dichotomy are all retired: the bound is the knob, the rate follows from residual entropy.
proposals.why_it_wins: It removes the exact mechanism that costs TRACQ 3-5 orders of magnitude. Open-loop cumprod error is a multiplicative random walk (RMSE ~ sqrt(t)*sigma_q*|X|, diverging to 3.8e95 on MetroPT-3); the lattice construction makes per-point error <= eps with zero accumulation — the same guarantee class as SZ3 abs mode and ZFP tolerance mode. Information-theoretically it also fixes the rate side: instead of mu-law spreading 256 levels uniformly (near-incompressible for DEFLATE), the difference image d concentrates around 0 for any signal smoother than white noise, so the entropy stage finally has skew to exploit. It converts TRACQ from 'no error bound, unbounded drift' to 'user-specified abs/rel bound, provable', which is the headline feature reviewers compared it against SZ3/ZFP on.
proposals.expected_gain: UCI Air Quality (13 vars x 9357 steps): at eps_abs=0.007, RMSE = eps/sqrt(3) ~ 0.004 (matching ZFP tol=1e-1's measured 0.004) with expected 6-10 bits/sample after Zstd on the difference image, i.e. ratio 0.10-0.18 vs ZFP's 0.273 — TRACQ wins the rate-distortion point it currently loses by 27000x in RMSE (108.3 -> ~0.004). MetroPT-3: divergence eliminated by construction; at eps_abs=1.0 (RMSE ~0.58 < anchored TRACQ's 1.71) with slowly-varying plant sensors the difference image is mostly zeros, Zstd should reach 0.2-0.8 bits/sample, ratio ~0.004-0.015 vs anchored TRACQ's 0.0297 — strictly Pareto-dominating current TRACQ everywhere.
proposals.implementation_sketch: New class in tracq/core_enhanced.py (or core_eb.py), ~120 lines. Encode: v = np.round(X/(2*eps)).astype(np.int64); d = np.diff(v, axis=1); store v[:,0] as float64 baseline analog in metadata (or as int64 lattice index). Small-residual mask: small = np.abs(d) <= 126; img = np.where(small, d+128, 255).astype(np.uint8) with 255 reserved as escape (see Proposal 3 for the sidecar). REL mode: sign = np.sign(X) (require positivity via existing _compute_value_offsets, reusing auto_offset); v = np.round(np.log(np.abs(X)+tiny)/np.log1p(2*eps_rel)). Decode: d = img.astype(np.int64)-128 with escapes patched from sidecar; v = np.concatenate([v0[:,None], v0[:,None]+np.cumsum(d,axis=1)], axis=1); X_hat = 2*eps*v. Container: existing ImageCodec.save_png for the uint8 image unchanged; add eps, mode, v0 to the tracq_meta JSON. Benchmark by adding an 'eps sweep' to scripts/rate_distortion.py mirroring zfp_sweep/sz3_sweep so RD curves are directly comparable.
proposals.risk: REL/log mode fails on zero-crossing channels (log undefined) — must fall back to ABS lattice per channel (Proposal 4), otherwise the near-zero pathology returns in a new costume. int64 lattice indices can be huge if eps is tiny relative to data magnitude (e.g. eps=1e-6 on O(1e6) values gives ~40-bit indices); harmless for cumsum but the first-column storage and sidecar must use int64, not float, to keep exactness. On white-noise-dominated channels the difference image has high entropy and the ratio win over 16-bit TRACQ shrinks — but RMSE is still bounded, so the method never loses the distortion axis. Honest benchmarking risk: must count metadata + sidecar bytes in the ratio.
proposals.interactions: Prerequisite for every other proposal: 2 and 5 predict on the integer lattice this creates; 3 is its escape mechanism; 4 tunes its bin widths. CONFLICTS: mu-law must be disabled in this mode (companding destroys the uniform-bin error bound); anchors become dead weight (drift is zero) — remove them from the EB path and from the paper's story. The existing auto_offset machinery is REUSED (not deleted) to make channels positive for REL mode.
proposals.preserves_image_artifact: The stored grid is still (n_vars x n_time-1), one pixel per variable per timestep — it IS the relative-change grid, now on a principled multiplicative lattice. Rendered as uint8 centered at 128 it is arguably MORE viewable than the mu-law grid: flat mid-gray background, bright/dark pixels exactly where the signal moves, escape pixels (255) highlight anomalies for free. Compressed-domain anomaly detection improves because pixel intensity is now monotone in true relative change with known scale.

proposals.name: Escape-coded exact-outlier sidecar (SZ-style unpredictable-point fallback)
proposals.mechanism: Reserve one uint8 code (255) in the difference image as an escape marker. Any pixel whose lattice residual d[i,t] falls outside [-126, +127] — large jumps, sensor spikes, regime changes, channels where eps is tight relative to volatility — is stored exactly in a sparse sidecar: positions as np.flatnonzero(~small) (delta-encoded uint32) plus the raw int64 residuals (or, simpler and fully exact, the raw float64 values X[i,t] re-snapped to the lattice at decode). At decode, escapes are patched into d before the cumsum, so exactness of the integer cumsum — and therefore the global error bound — is preserved through outliers. This replaces the clamp (which currently DESTROYS outliers with unbounded error) and the near-zero offset heuristics' failure modes.
proposals.why_it_wins: This is the half of SZ3 that makes its bound a guarantee rather than an average: prediction+quantization handles the predictable 99.x% of points at <2 bits each, and the unpredictable remainder is stored exactly so max-error <= eps holds for EVERY point. TRACQ currently has the worst of both worlds: it pays full rate for every point AND has unbounded error at clipped points. Rate math: if q is the escape fraction, sidecar cost ~ q*(4+8) bytes/point; for q<1% that is <1 bit/point amortized — negligible against the 8-10x error-bound credibility it buys. It is also the correct fix for failure mode 4 (near-zero channels): a near-zero channel in ABS mode simply produces a few escapes instead of a blown-up percent-change column.
proposals.expected_gain: No direct RMSE change at fixed eps (the bound already holds via Proposal 1), but it is what makes max_error <= eps TRUE on real data — the metric zfp_sweep/sz3_sweep already report (max_error column in baselines.py) and where current TRACQ shows unbounded values. Enables honest 'error-bounded' claims in the paper. Rate cost on UCI Air Quality at eps giving q~0.5% escapes: ~+0.06 bits/sample (~+1% ratio). On spike-heavy MetroPT-3 channels it AVOIDS the alternative costs: without it you either widen eps for everyone (RMSE up ~10x) or use uint16 pixels (rate up 2x).
proposals.implementation_sketch: In the encoder from Proposal 1: small = np.abs(d) <= 126; img = np.where(small, d+128, 255).astype(np.uint8); esc_pos = np.flatnonzero(~small.ravel()).astype(np.uint32); esc_val = d.ravel()[~small.ravel()].astype(np.int64); sidecar = zstd.compress(np.diff(esc_pos, prepend=0).tobytes() + esc_val.tobytes()). Store sidecar length in metadata; append sidecar bytes after the PNG (or as a second tEXt/zTXt chunk via ImageCodec, or as a second member in the Zstd container). Decode: d = img.astype(np.int64) - 128; d.ravel()[np.cumsum(esc_pos_deltas)] = esc_val; proceed with cumsum. ~40 lines. Count sidecar bytes in all ratio computations.
proposals.risk: If eps is set aggressively small on a noisy channel, the escape fraction q can explode (10-50%), and the sidecar (12 bytes/escape) makes the ratio worse than just using a uint16 index image — mitigate with a per-variable rule: if predicted q_i > 3% (measurable at encode time from the d histogram, before committing), switch that variable to a 16-bit index row or widen its bin via Proposal 4. Two-part artifact (image + sidecar) slightly complicates the container, but codec.py's tEXt-chunk pattern already sets the precedent for auxiliary data inside the PNG.
proposals.interactions: Pure complement to Proposal 1 (it is the mechanism that makes the bound universal) and to Proposal 2 (escapes are computed on the post-prediction residual, so better predictors reduce q). Replaces adaptive clamp entirely — clamping and escaping are mutually exclusive philosophies; keep only the escape. Synergy with Proposal 4: the q_i statistic is the natural driver for per-variable bin/bit-depth decisions.
proposals.preserves_image_artifact: The image stays a dense per-timestep uint8 grid; escape pixels render as maximum-brightness dots, which is a feature for visual inspection — spikes and regime changes literally light up. The sidecar is invisible metadata, exactly like the existing baseline/clamp JSON in the tEXt chunk; the PNG remains openable in any viewer.

proposals.name: Lattice-domain prediction family: order-2 temporal + 2D Lorenzo, per-variable selection, Zstd-first entropy stage
proposals.mechanism: Between lattice quantization and the image, insert an integer-exact prediction step chosen per variable (row): P0: store v (RLE-friendly constants); P1: d1 = diff(v) (current default); P2: d2[t] = v[t] - 2v[t-1] + v[t-2] (delta-of-delta, Gorilla/SZ-Lorenzo-order-2 analog); PL: 2D Lorenzo on the correlation-reordered grid, r[i,t] = v[i,t] - v[i,t-1] - v[i-1,t] + v[i-1,t-1], exploiting cross-channel correlation (reuses _compute_variable_order). All predictors are integer-linear, so decoding is exact integer cumsum/prefix operations in numpy (P2 = double cumsum; PL = cumsum along t then along i). Selection: compute each candidate's residual byte histogram entropy per row (vectorized, ~4 passes) and pick argmin; store 2-bit choice per row in metadata. Entropy stage: keep PNG (filters off or 'Up' only) as the VIEW artifact, but make the MEASURED compressed size zstd(level 19) over the residual image bytes + sidecar — the existing Zstd container path in the repo — because Zstd's FSE handles the peaked residual distribution ~15-30% better than DEFLATE's Huffman with its suboptimal filter heuristics.
proposals.why_it_wins: This is SZ3's actual rate engine: the error bound fixes distortion, prediction fixes rate. For smooth or trending series, first differences still carry the trend (nonzero mean, wide support); second differences remove it, typically cutting residual entropy 1.5-3 bits/sample. For the multivariate case, TRACQ's own premise — correlated variables — is currently exploited only via PNG row reordering; 2D Lorenzo uses it directly in the residual domain, which is worth another 0.5-2 bits on strongly co-moving channels (the 13 UCI air-quality sensors co-move on diurnal cycles). Since RMSE is pinned at eps/sqrt(3) regardless, every bit saved is pure ratio improvement, moving TRACQ from ZFP-competitive to SZ3-competitive.
proposals.expected_gain: At fixed RMSE (set by eps), expect ratio improvements of 1.5-2.5x on UCI Air Quality (d1 entropy ~7-9 bits -> best-of-family ~4-6 bits/sample) and 2-4x on MetroPT-3's slowly-varying channels (d2/PL residuals mostly zero -> long zero runs -> Zstd RLE takes bits/sample below 0.5). Combined with Proposal 1's numbers: UCI ratio ~0.06-0.10 at RMSE 0.004 (vs ZFP 0.273, SZ3 typically ~0.04-0.08 at that RMSE on similar data) — i.e. within ~1.3x of SZ3 and clearly ahead of ZFP; finally far below the lossless Delta+Zstd floor of 0.12-0.24, answering failure mode 3.
proposals.implementation_sketch: Encoder: v (int64) from Proposal 1; candidates = {0: v-v0_broadcast, 1: np.diff(v,axis=1), 2: np.diff(v,n=2,axis=1), 3: lorenzo2d(v[order])}; for each row compute H = -sum(p*log2(p)) over np.bincount of np.clip(cand+128,0,255) (escapes counted at ~13 bytes); choice = argmin. Decode P2: v = np.cumsum(np.cumsum(d2,axis=1),axis=1) + affine terms from the two stored initial lattice values per row; PL: v = np.cumsum(np.cumsum(r,axis=1),axis=0) + first-row/first-column stored as P1 rows. ~150 lines incl. tests that decode(encode(x)) meets the bound exactly. Entropy: reuse the repo's existing zstandard container path for the honest size; PNG saved alongside for the artifact. Keep predictor choice OUT of the hot loop — it is 4 vectorized histogram passes.
proposals.risk: P2 and PL amplify escape counts at spikes (a single jump perturbs 2-3 residuals), so predictor selection must include the sidecar cost in its objective, not just dense entropy — otherwise it picks P2 on spiky rows and loses. 2D Lorenzo depends on the greedy correlation ordering (already implemented but marked experimental); a bad ordering makes PL worse than P1, which the per-row argmin safely handles. Bookkeeping of initial conditions per predictor order is fiddly (off-by-one on row starts) — property-test with random integer grids for exact round-trip. Gains are data-dependent: on white-noise channels all predictors tie and the win is ~0.
proposals.interactions: Multiplies Proposal 1's rate win; feeds Proposal 3 (escape fraction depends on predictor choice, so select jointly). Subsumes the existing reorder_variables feature (PL is its principled version) and the Gorilla baseline's delta-of-delta idea (P2), so the paper can claim a superset. If Proposal 5 (block transform) is implemented, it competes as a 5th candidate in this same per-row/per-block selection framework rather than as a separate mode.
proposals.preserves_image_artifact: Residual grid stays (n_vars x n_time-1)-shaped, one pixel per timestep, centered at 128 — still a viewable grayscale image (P2/PL residual images look like edge-detected versions of the change grid, which is if anything MORE diagnostic: anomalies are the only non-gray pixels). Metadata records the per-row predictor so any pixel remains interpretable as a quantized change with a known linear reconstruction; a 'render as d1' debug view (one integer cumsum) can regenerate the classic change image losslessly for inspection.

proposals.name: Per-variable domain and bin allocation (mixed abs/rel bounds, RD-driven bit depth)
proposals.mechanism: Make the lattice per-variable instead of global. Each variable i gets: (a) a DOMAIN — log-lattice if min|X_i| stays safely positive (relative bound eps_rel, preserving the pure 'relative change' semantics), else absolute lattice (eps_abs,i); (b) a BIN WIDTH — user gives one global target (e.g. rel=1e-3 with abs floor), mapped per channel as eps_i = max(eps_abs_floor, eps_rel * scale_i) where scale_i is the channel's magnitude (percentile of |X_i|), mirroring SZ3's 'rel' mode which scales the bound by the data range; (c) a BIT DEPTH — uint8 row with escapes vs uint16 row, chosen by the measured escape fraction q_i and residual entropy from Proposal 3's histogram (the same statistic). All parameters land in the existing per-variable metadata pattern (clamps are already per-variable lists in metadata, so the container needs no schema change).
proposals.why_it_wins: Multivariate sensor data spans wildly different magnitudes (UCI: CO ~ O(1), PT08 sensors ~ O(1000)); a single global eps_abs either wastes bits on large channels or wrecks small ones — this is why SZ3 ships abs/rel/psnr modes rather than one knob. Rate-distortion optimality for independent channels under a sum-rate constraint requires equalizing marginal RD slopes, which per-channel bins approximate at zero algorithmic cost. Empirically this is the difference between 'wins on aggregate RMSE but loses per-channel SMAPE/rho' (a likely reviewer complaint, and SMAPE/rho are already in the metrics suite) and winning across the whole metrics table. It also finishes the near-zero story properly: channels that cross zero get the ABS lattice, no heuristic 2*|min| offsets needed.
proposals.expected_gain: At fixed aggregate rate, per-channel bounds typically buy 2-5x RMSE improvement on the WORST channel and 10-30% overall ratio at fixed per-channel error targets versus a global bin (standard result when channel variances span >=2 orders of magnitude, which UCI's do at ~3 orders). Concretely: global eps_abs=0.007 sized for CO wastes ~7 bits/sample on the O(1000) PT08 channels where eps=0.7 would satisfy the same relative fidelity — per-channel binning reclaims those bits, dropping UCI ratio from ~0.08 to ~0.05-0.06 at unchanged per-channel relative error. SMAPE and Pearson rho columns improve on every small-magnitude channel.
proposals.implementation_sketch: ~60 lines on top of Proposals 1-3: compute per-variable stats (min, min|x|, percentile magnitude — the code for this exists in _compute_value_offsets and _compute_adaptive_clamps and is repurposed, not rewritten); eps_vec = np.maximum(eps_abs_floor, eps_rel*np.percentile(np.abs(X),99,axis=1)); v = np.round(X/(2*eps_vec[:,None])).astype(np.int64) (or log-lattice rows where safe_positive); metadata gains 'domain':[...], 'eps':[...] lists exactly like today's per-variable 'clamp_pct'. Bit-depth choice: rows with q_i>3% stored in a separate uint16 PNG plane or packed as two uint8 rows (document in metadata). Benchmark: rerun the RD sweep with the single user knob (target rel error) to produce one clean curve per dataset.
proposals.risk: Per-variable eps makes 'RMSE at ratio X' comparisons subtler — the paper must report per-channel normalized error (SMAPE/NRMSE) alongside aggregate RMSE or reviewers will suspect knob-tuning; the metrics suite already computes these, so report them. Mixed uint8/uint16 rows complicate the single-image story (mitigation: keep everything uint8+escapes, accept higher q on hard channels — simpler and usually within 10% of optimal). Log-lattice channels have relative, not absolute, bounds — the max_error column must be computed per the promised bound type or the guarantee claim will be falsified by the benchmark script.
proposals.interactions: Pure parameterization layer over Proposals 1-3; no conflicts. Uses Proposal 3's escape statistics as its allocation signal. Replaces _compute_adaptive_clamps and the auto_offset near-zero heuristics wholesale — retire them in the EB path. Gives the paper the user-facing 'abs OR rel error bound' API that the brief lists as a missing feature versus SZ3/ZFP.
proposals.preserves_image_artifact: Grid shape and per-timestep resolution unchanged; each row is still 'quantized relative (or absolute) change per timestep'. Because bins are per-row, pixel intensity means 'k bins of that variable's step' — visually consistent within each row, which is how humans read heatmaps anyway (row-wise). The metadata fully determines each row's physical scale, so the codec module's viewer/tooling can annotate rows with their eps, and cross-row visual comparability can be restored in the viewer by optional row normalization at display time (display-only, does not touch stored data).

proposals.name: Blockwise reversible transform on the residual grid (ZFP-style decorrelation) — prototype-and-keep-only-if-it-wins
proposals.mechanism: Partition the (reordered) integer residual grid into 4x4 blocks (4 variables x 4 timesteps) and apply ZFP's lifted, integer-friendly near-orthogonal transform (the 4-point ZFP lifting: x+=w; w>>=1 style butterfly sequence, implementable exactly in int64 numpy with shifts along each axis) BEFORE the entropy stage, as a 5th candidate in Proposal 2's per-block selection. Coefficients are stored (offset to uint8/uint16 with escapes) in the same grid positions, so the artifact stays a dense per-timestep image of transform coefficients; decode inverts the lifting exactly in integers, then proceeds with the usual inverse prediction and lattice mapping. Selection per block-row by measured entropy, exactly like Proposal 2's predictor choice, so it can never make the codec worse than not using it.
proposals.why_it_wins: This is the honest test of whether ZFP's core trick adds anything once SZ3's core trick is in place. ZFP's advantage on smooth fields is that the block transform compacts energy into few coefficients and bit-plane coding spends bits where they matter. On the lattice-residual grid, most of that decorrelation has ALREADY been done by prediction (P2/PL leave near-white residuals on predictable data), so the expected additional gain is modest — but on quasi-periodic or oscillatory channels (diurnal cycles in air quality, rotating-machinery harmonics in MetroPT-3) linear prediction underfits and a transform captures the oscillation in 1-2 coefficients per block where d2 leaves a full-amplitude sinusoid. Including it (a) covers the signal class where 1-3 lose to ZFP, (b) gives the paper a clean ablation ('SZ-style prediction vs ZFP-style transform inside the same grid framework'), which is a genuinely novel comparison and strengthens the contribution narrative independent of raw numbers.
proposals.expected_gain: Smallest and least certain of the five: expect 0-20% additional ratio at fixed RMSE, concentrated on oscillation-dominated channels; expect ~0% (and automatic non-selection) on trend/noise channels. On UCI Air Quality's strongly diurnal sensors, plausibly 10-15% over Proposal 2 alone. If the measured gain is <5% overall, drop it from the codec and report the ablation in the paper — negative results about transform-vs-prediction on 1D sensor grids are still publishable support for the design choice.
proposals.implementation_sketch: ~120 lines: implement ZFP's 4-point forward/inverse lifting as int64 numpy ops applied via reshape to (..., nblocks, 4) along time then variables (pad edges; store pad amounts in metadata); verify exact integer invertibility with property tests (this is the critical correctness gate — use the published lifting steps which are exactly reversible in two's-complement arithmetic). Register as candidate 4 in Proposal 2's selection with the same entropy+escape-cost objective. Zigzag-order coefficients within blocks before byte packing so low-frequency coefficients cluster for Zstd. Benchmark via the same eps-sweep harness.
proposals.risk: Highest implementation risk of the five: an inexact lifting implementation silently breaks the error bound (transform must be bit-exact reversible over int64, including overflow behavior — clamp block inputs or use int64 headroom checks). Transform coefficients have larger dynamic range than residuals, raising escape rates — must account for that in selection cost. Very plausible outcome is 'never selected, delete it'; time-box the prototype. Do NOT attempt ZFP's bit-plane embedded coding stage — it cannot be expressed as a viewable dense image and duplicates what Zstd already does adequately here.
proposals.interactions: Competes with (never stacks on) P2/PL within Proposal 2's per-block selection — the selection framework makes it strictly additive-or-neutral. Depends on Proposal 1's integer lattice for exact invertibility. Increases Proposal 3's escape traffic on selected blocks (include in cost). Irrelevant to Proposal 4. If cut, nothing else changes — it is the only fully optional module.
proposals.preserves_image_artifact: Coefficient blocks occupy the same (n_vars x n_time-1) grid, so the PNG remains a dense per-timestep image; transformed blocks render as textured 4x4 tiles (like a JPEG coefficient view). For human inspection the codec keeps the pre-transform residual view reproducible exactly (inverse lifting is lossless), so the viewer can always display the canonical change-grid image; per-timestep temporal resolution is untouched since blocks tile the grid without downsampling.
